title: Every Pipeline Blocked by a State Lock
intro: All Terraform pipelines have been failing for an hour with 'Error acquiring the state lock'. Nobody on the team thinks they're running anything.

steps.prompt: Run a plan to see the full lock error, including who holds it.
steps.fake_output:
Error: Error acquiring the state lock

Lock Info:
  ID:        9f2c-44e1-b7a0
  Path:      my-tf-state/prod/terraform.tfstate
  Operation: OperationTypeApply
  Who:       runner@ci-runner-7
  Created:   2026-09-27 09:02:11 UTC
steps.hint: The lock info tells you exactly which machine and operation acquired it, and when.

steps.prompt: The lock was taken by an apply on ci-runner-7 over an hour ago. Check that pipeline's runs to see whether that apply is actually still running.
steps.fake_output:
STATUS     NAME           WORKFLOW        EVENT  ELAPSED
cancelled  apply prod     terraform.yml   push   2m14s   (09:02)
steps.hint: Confirm the lock holder is really dead before touching the lock.

steps.prompt: That run was cancelled mid-apply at 09:04 — it died without releasing its lock. Before unlocking, verify state is intact by pulling it.
steps.hint: Always take a backup before any lock or state surgery.

steps.fake_output: Terraform state has been successfully unlocked!
steps.hint: Use the exact lock ID from the error message.

steps.prompt: The cancelled apply may have left things half-done. Run a plan to see what reality looks like now.
steps.fake_output:
# aws_instance.worker[2] will be created
Plan: 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
steps.hint: An interrupted apply often leaves some resources created and others not.

resolution: A pipeline run was cancelled halfway through an apply. Cancelling killed Terraform before it could release its state lock, so every later run was blocked. force-unlock was safe here ONLY because the run was confirmed dead — unlocking a lock held by a still-running apply allows two concurrent writes, which is exactly how state gets corrupted. The post-unlock plan also showed the interrupted apply had created 2 of 3 workers; finishing with a normal apply reconciles that. Process fixes: configure CI so Terraform receives a graceful interrupt (SIGINT) on cancel rather than being killed, serialize applies per environment with a pipeline concurrency group, and treat 'cancel during apply' as something to avoid rather than a routine action.
